children: , the cloud and enterprise-AI giant, opened its new three-zone India South Central cloud region, putting Hyderabad deeper into the company's global AI infrastructure map. Shares traded at $496.905, The bigger story is not another data-center pin on the map. Microsoft is building local computing capacity where Indian banks, conglomerates and digital platforms increasingly want AI performance without sending sensitive workloads outside the country.

The Hyderabad region is Microsoft's fourth cloud region in India, with Adani Group, Bajaj Finserv, HDFC Bank and PB Pay already participating in trials. The infrastructure is designed to support sovereign-cloud requirements and Indian data residency while using effectively zero water for cooling. That combination matters. Microsoft is selling customers more than raw computing power: local availability, regulatory flexibility and lower dependence on distant regions can make Azure harder to replace for enterprises running mission-critical AI workloads.

Microsoft's $20.5 billion commitment spans a much broader India investment program rather than this facility alone, and management has not disclosed the Hyderabad region's megawatt capacity, server count or revenue target. That leaves utilization as the number investors should watch. The valuation picture adds an interesting counterweight: the shares at $496.905 sit 15.28% below the $586.56 GF Value estimate. In other words, the market price is currently well below GuruFocus' intrinsic-value benchmark, while Microsoft is still pouring capital into one of the world's fastest-growing markets for cloud and AI infrastructure.

title: Microsoft Drops as Three-Zone Hyderabad Region Goes Live
